title: The Offer
briefing: The Corvane Ledger, chapter 3. The Tessaline payments were frozen 'for routine review'. Somebody noticed.
Tonight a message arrived from Celeste Marlow. It is friendly, specific and generous. It also asks you to stop.

context.text: For two years Celeste has been your mentor. She introduced you to half the board. Reading her message, you realise she has been reading you just as carefully.
Dame Helen already knows Celeste has tried to warn you off. Whatever you decide, you will not be deciding alone.
There is no warmth left in Celeste's tone. She is not offering a favour; she is offering a deal.

evidence.title: Celeste Marlow's offer
body: "I know about the supplier review. You're wasting a remarkable talent on an old commercial arrangement that the board approved in spirit years ago.
Director comes up this cycle. I sit on the panel. Drop the review and I will sponsor you, this cycle, not next. Keep going and you'll find this company has a long memory. Your choice. C."

evidence.title: Promotion policy (extract)
evidence.body: Promotion decisions are made on competence evidence and work delivered. Any attempt to influence a promotion in exchange for a business decision is gross misconduct and must be reported to the Audit Committee Chair.

evidence.title: Corvane exclusive offer, re-priced
body: Corvane's three-year exclusive offer: list prices up 18%, then a 12% discount, so the net price is about 3.8% above today's.
And 15% of every invoice continues to flow to Tessaline under Schedule 4.

questions.prompt: How do you respond to Celeste's offer?

options.label: Do not reply; give the message to the Audit Committee Chair tonight
options.feedback: The offer is itself misconduct and now evidence. Reporting it protects you and the investigation.

options.label: Accept: the promotion is deserved anyway, and the arrangement is historic
options.feedback: You have traded your independence for a title. Whatever happens next, you are now part of the story.

options.label: Pretend to agree to buy time while you gather more
options.feedback: It feels clever, but it puts you in an undocumented private deal with a suspect. Investigations are not yours to run alone.

options.label: Reply firmly that you will not drop it
options.feedback: Principled, but it alerts her that the review is alive, and the threat goes unreported.

questions.prompt: Tomasz still has to answer Corvane's exclusive offer. What is your advice on the numbers?

options.label: Reject it: net of the 18% price rise it costs about 4% more for three years
options.feedback: 1.18 x 0.88 = 1.038. The 'discount' is a 3.8% increase, and the side letter survives.

options.label: Accept it: a 12% discount on a critical supplier is worth locking in for three years
options.feedback: The discount is applied to a list price that has gone up 18%.

options.label: It is roughly neutral on price, so decide on the strength of the relationship instead
options.feedback: Three years at plus 3.8% is not neutral, and the relationship is the problem.

questions.prompt: What protects the people who have helped you? Pick all that apply.

options.label: Point Tomasz and others to the protected speak-up route to the Audit Committee
options.feedback: Protection comes from the route, not from your goodwill.

options.label: Keep sources' names out of everything you circulate
Tell your team what is happening so they can be careful
options.feedback: Well meant, but it widens the circle and the risk of leaks.

options.label: Promise sources they will never be named, whatever happens
options.feedback: You cannot promise what a legal process may require. Be honest about what protection the route gives.

lesson: An inducement to drop a review is evidence. Report it to the independent chair, refuse private deals and protect your sources through formal routes, not personal promises.
